subject: Hiring constituency review — req shelf & reallocation proposal
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: Kelly Morris <kelly@talentpartners.com>
Date: 2027-10-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hiring constituency review — req shelf & reallocation proposal

Team —

As we prep for the QBR next week, I ran the req roster through the capacity & impact worksheet (attached). We need a short, decisive headcount action to keep runway while protecting critical customer-facing commitments. Proposed plan (high level):

1) Temporarily shelf 6 non-customer-facing software reqs (platform and infra still covered at minimal sustain level). See tab "Shelf Candidates" in the attached workbook.
2) Reallocate two already-approved offers (when they accept) from infra-to-data/feature work to accelerate the inference cost-optimization roadmap — these hires can be cross-trained and reduce near-term external compute spend.
3) Approve 2 immediate backfills for CS/Support roles that are directly tied to the Acme renewal (we have a renewal play starting Jan).

Rationale: preserves customer SLAs while saving ~0.9 FTE-months of burn for Q4; helps avoid broad hiring freeze escalation to the exec team. If we can't get leadership alignment, we default to a stricter hiring freeze and push more product work to next year.

Action items I need from each of you by EOD tomorrow:
- Soojin: review the shelf candidates and flag any positions that are mission-critical (I marked two as "do not shelf" but want your confirm).
- Markus: confirm whether the reallocation approach is acceptable from an OKR/roadmap standpoint.
- Vanessa: prioritization on the CS backfills (which two req IDs to greenlight).
- Jordan: rough delta to Q4 run-rate and whether finance can support the 2 backfills as a carve-out.

Attachments: req-shelf-worksheet-2027Q4.xlsx (worksheet), capacity-impact-brief.csv

Thanks — short thread preferred; I will synthesize for QBR pack.

— Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, markus.klein@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-03T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hiring constituency review — req shelf & reallocation proposal

Evelyn — thanks for the clear summary and the worksheet. Quick notes after a skim:

- I agree with shelving the six candidates except: Req #PL-214 (edge runtime engineer) should stay open — we have two critical infra bugs that block a customer deployment that Acme flagged last week. I marked it "hold" in the sheet and added a short rationale.
- The two roles you propose to reallocate are acceptable, but we should explicitly commit to a 3-month cross-training plan in their offer letters (so the hiring manager budgets onboarding time).

I'll signal to hiring managers today on the hold/shelf flags.

Sooj
Soojin Lee
Director, Engineering Planning

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, soojin.lee@redwood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-03T13:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hiring constituency review — req shelf & reallocation proposal

+1 to Evelyn and Soojin with one caveat: the reallocation construct can go forward only if Product agrees to a temporary scope shift for the hires (feature deferral). I'm okay with the trade if we get a written nod from Product owners by Friday. I'll block that as a contingency in the QBR slide.

Also, please ensure we don't create an optics issue for Dedicated customers — if Acme is sensitive, let's proactively loop their CSM (Sarah Turner) so they see the plan. Evelyn, if you want, loop Sarah on the single-line note.

Markus
Markus Klein
GM, Customer & GTM Ops

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, soojin.lee@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, jordan.blake@redwood.com
Cc: Sarah Turner <sarah.turner@acme.com>
Date: 2027-10-04T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hiring constituency review — req shelf & reallocation proposal

Evelyn — I reviewed the backfill asks with CS leadership this morning. Recommend we greenlight the two CS backfills tied to Acme: Req CS-098 (Renewals Manager) and CS-112 (Technical Account Specialist). Those are the two roles that directly influence the renewal health score and escalation SLA.

Sarah — looping you so you're aware we've marked these as high-priority backfills to protect the Jan renewal. If there are specific skills we should prioritize in the job brief (e.g., Python/SOAP experience, account escalation history), please share by EOD Friday and we'll include it in the req.

Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Customer Success

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, soojin.lee@redwood.com, markus.klein@reduswood.com, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com
Date: 2027-10-04T15:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hiring constituency review — req shelf & reallocation proposal

Evelyn — finance view: Q4 run-rate reduction from shelving the six non-customer-facing reqs is estimated at $185k (salary + on-costs). Carve-out for 2 CS backfills increases run-rate by $56k. Net savings ~ $129k for Q4 — acceptable to keep runway conservative.

Two asks before I sign off for the pack:
1) A brief line item in the QBR pack listing the six shelved req IDs and the two held (so finance can audit).
2) Confirmation that the reallocated offers will be documented with the cross-training plan (so we can treat them as internal cost neutral from a headcount plan perspective).

If you provide those by EOD, I'll annotate the QBR slides and mark as finance-approved.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Finance Business Partner
